title: Burst capacity auctioning and credit reconciliation workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a robust mechanism to allocate short-term surplus GPU capacity to tenants in a fair, predictable way while making overage charges and credit reconciliation transparent. Current transient-burst behavior is reactive and opaque for customers; this ticket proposes an auction-style allocation combined with an epoch-based reconciliation ledger that preserves throughput guarantees for committed capacity and offers controlled, priced access to spare capacity.

Goals:
- Enable controlled short-term access to spare capacity with deterministic prioritization and pricing signals.
- Maintain Dedicated capacity SLOs for reserved tenants; auctioning must be preemptible and have defined preemption semantics.
- Produce clear invoice line items and a reconciliation window that converts temporary usage into either consumed credits or amortized overage charges.
- Surface telemetry and cost signals to customers and support teams so burst behavior is explainable and actionable.

Design overview:
1) Epoch-based allocation: Split burst allocation into fixed epochs (e.g., 10-minute windows). During each epoch, spare capacity is offered into a short auction. Tenants may bid using a burst credit balance or a max-price-per-token override. Winning bids get exclusive access to a fraction of spare pool for that epoch.
2) Priority tiers: Three priority tiers — Reserved (no auction), Premium-bid, and Best-effort. Reserved tenant requests always satisfy reserved pools first. Premium-bid wins against Best-effort; ties broken by credit age and recent usage smoothing.
3) Credit flow and reconciliation: Tenants can 1) consume pre-purchased burst credits, 2) use live-bid funds billed at epoch close, or 3) accept post-usage amortized overage. At the end of each reconciliation window (24 hours by default) we collapse epochs to invoice items: consumed credits, auction charges, or amortized overage. A transparent ledger is exposed in Console and exportable via billing API.
4) Preemption and graceful degrade: When spare capacity is reclaimed, winning allocations receive a preemption notice with a short grace period (configurable: default 30s) so client SDKs can reduce batch sizes or fallback to lower-cost model variants.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Auction vs simple price-tier: Auctioning lets price-sensitive tenants self-select into spare capacity while yielding higher utilization. Simpler fixed-price pools would be easier operationally but less efficient at extracting willingness-to-pay during short spikes.
- Epoch length: Short epochs (<=5m) increase responsiveness but raise scheduling churn; we picked 10m as initial compromise.
- Reconciliation window: Immediate billing increases transparency but is noisy for customers; daily reconciliation balances real-time feedback with clean invoice items.

Telemetry and observability:
We will emit the following metrics per-tenant and per-pool: epoch_bid_attempts, epoch_bid_wins, epoch_allocated_seconds, preemptions_count, preemption_latency_ms, credits_consumed, auction_charge_cents, amortized_overage_cents. Console will show a per-epoch timeline and a 24h reconciliation summary. Alerts: >3 preemptions in 10m (possible QoS issue), auction win with >80% preemption rate (bad for tenant experience).

API & Console surfaces:
- Billing API: /billing/burst-ledger?start=...&end=... returns per-epoch ledger entries (consumed_credits, auction_price, allocated_seconds).
- Console: new “Burst ledger” panel under Dedicated -> Capacity -> Burst explaining per-epoch allocations and resulting invoice items with drilldowns to request traces.

Migration & rollout plan:
Phase 1 (canary): internal-only auction for non-critical tenants + telemetry collection (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for customers with burst credits enabled, UI in Console + opt-in billing terms (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default for new Dedicated fleets, migration tooling for legacy burst consumers (6–8 weeks).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Fine-tune epoch length per region/hardware class (NVIDIA H100 vs A100 behavior).
- UX for customers to view projected auction costs before bidding.
- Legal/billing: whether auction charges should be refundable in post-charge disputes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Auction allocator running in canary region with telemetry and no regression to reserved SLOs.
- Console shows per-epoch ledger and reconciliation summary.
- Billing exports match ledger and produce readable invoice line items.
- Preemption signals delivered within 30s and SDK demos graceful fallback.

notes: This ticket focuses on allocation and billing workflow; separate performance-tuning tickets will address kernel-level latency when running auctions at high QPS.
qa_checklist: Canary epoch runs without reserved SLO regression
Console ledger matches exported billing CSV
SDK receives preemption callback and fallback test passes
postmortem_on_failure: If canary leads to SLO regression, pause auctioning and run immediate rollback; create incident with RCA within 72 hours.
